keyVerseText: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
rootMeaning: The word αὐγή (augḗ) lacks a clear etymology, but its core meaning centers on the concept of light emanating at the break of day. Beyond the simple English gloss of 'break of day,' it conveys the vivid image of rays or beams of sunlight that signal the dawn, embodying both physical brightness and the metaphorical emergence of life and visibility. This root sense enriches the understanding of the term by emphasizing the dynamic and radiant quality of early morning light rather than merely a point in time.
usageInScripture: αὐγή is used sparingly in the New Testament, appearing only once in Acts 20:11, where it is translated as 'break of day.' This singular occurrence highlights the moment of dawn as a significant temporal marker. The lexicon and concordance information show that αὐγή consistently denotes the first light of the sun or dawn, often associated with life and clarity. Its usage underscores the transition from darkness to light, both literally and figuratively.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, αὐγή symbolizes the arrival of divine illumination and new beginnings, reflecting God's role as the source of light and life. In Scripture, light frequently represents truth, holiness, and the presence of God, making the break of day an apt metaphor for spiritual awakening and resurrection hope. Recognizing αὐγή as the radiant dawn invites believers to see Christ as the true Light who dispels darkness and brings life. This word thus deepens our appreciation of God's faithfulness in bringing light after darkness and guiding His people into the fullness of life.
keyVerseReflection: In Acts 20:11, the phrase 'even till break of day' (αὐγή) marks the time until which Paul conversed after breaking bread, emphasizing the continuity and intensity of fellowship and teaching through the night into the first light. The use of αὐγή here not only situates the event in time but also metaphorically suggests the dawning of new understanding and spiritual illumination that comes through prolonged engagement with the Word. This highlights the transformative power of Christian fellowship sustained until the light of dawn.
